simple.meaning: אׇחֳרָן (ʼochŏrân) is a Hebrew object word meaning “other.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Daniel 2:11. The surrounding context includes kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אׇחֳרָן (H321) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: אׇחֳרָן (ʼochŏrân) / H321 is traced through Daniel 2:11, Daniel 2:44, Daniel 3:29, Daniel 5:17 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: It is a rare thing that the king requires, and there is no other who can show it before the king, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.”

timeline.evidenceText: It is a rare thing that the king requires, and there is no other who can show it before the king, except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.”

“In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which will never be destroyed, nor will its sovereignty be left to another people; but it will break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it will stand forever.

Therefore I make a decree, that every people, nation, and language, which speak anything evil against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill; because there is no other god who is able to deliver like this.”
Then Daniel answered before the king, “Let your gifts be to yourself, and give your rewards to another. Nevertheless, I will read the writing to the king, and make known to him the interpretation.
As for the ten horns, ten kings will arise out of this kingdom. Another will arise after them; and he will be different from the former, and he will put down three kings.

definitions.full: H321. ochoran אָחֳרָן adjective masculine another (Egyptian Aramaic אחרן S-C D 11 +; Nabataean, Palmyrene id . (Lzb 212 ); ᵑ7 ; compare Syriac ); — Dan 2:11 , 44 ; 3:29 ; 4:5 ; Kt 5:17 ; 7:24 . The feminine in use is אָחֳרַי (Egyptian Aramaic אחרה , RÉS 246 ; ᵑ7 Talmud אוֺחְרִי (D § 20. 5 ); compare K § 61, 5 M § 87 d Nö Beitr.51 ), 2:39 א ׳מַלְכוּ , 2:39 ; 7:5-6 , 8 , 20 .
